sections.what_happened: Departing the White House Oct 23, Trump said: 'Iran is not able to do much now. And we could, if we wanted to, just take all of the oil. We could take the whole country.' At the Florida rally he added the US would turn its attention to Cuba after the Iran issue is complete (Oneindia). This EXTENDS the 'finish it off or let it wither' remarks already recorded in totw-20261024-1100-04: the new elements are the explicit 'whole country' annexation phrasing and the Cuba-next sequence. Counterweight already on record: White House spokeswoman Anna Kelly (totw-20261024-1300-02) says the US will NOT attack Iran at any time before the Nov 3 midterms, and Trump himself told reporters he knew nothing of Barrack's weekend-strike claim. Demand note: the social demand check this scan surfaced Ukraine-energy engagement, not Cuba-specific counts; demand 4 rests on the standing Tier-1 Iran demand + the debate-bait character of annexation rhetoric.
sections.what_verified: Trump's own on-record statements are the primary source; outlet carries (igihe, Oneindia, News18) are unregistered in the source registry and do NOT count as corroborating families.
sections.what_disputed: Kelly's no-attack-before-midterms line and Trump's own 'I don't know anything about it' on the weekend-strike claim both undercut reading this as an imminent-action announcement; Waltz's year-long-stalemate warning (1100-04) is the other counterweight. No troop-movement or order evidence accompanies the rhetoric.
sections.why_matters: Report the quote verbatim, then immediately pair it with Kelly's no-strike-before-midterms line -- the channel does not carry a US president's annexation talk as its own voice, and the contradiction IS the story. Cuba-next widens the frame: this is no longer one war, it is a sequence.
sections.context: Background: UPDATE to totw-20261024-1100-04 / 0700-02 (big-missed Oct 23) -- Trump: US 'could take the whole country' and 'take all of the oil'; Cuba is next after Iran

totw_analysis: Our read: Report the quote verbatim, then immediately pair it with Kelly's no-strike-before-midterms line -- the channel does not carry a US president's annexation talk as its own voice, and the contradiction IS the story. Cuba-next widens the frame: this is no longer one war, it is a sequence. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Is 'take the whole country' a negotiating threat to force a deal, or a statement of intent that makes a deal impossible?
